summary: Phase A INFRA half, docs and stubs only, nothing installed on the VPS. SPE-4789/4793: GREPTIME_* placement under /etc/substrate/substrate.env with the tailnet-forwarder-preferred / public-HTTPS-Basic-fallback order, plus OTEL / MCP-audit / evidence env names reserved as placeholders; gateway.env.example marks its GREPTIME_* copy TRANSITIONAL because substrate-mcp owns the store credential. SPE-4792: systemd oneshot+timer and cron sketch for the seat lease heartbeat with env names only, the TIMEOUT < INTERVAL <= TTL/3 invariant, and a read-only credential-free drift-probe.sh feeding coord.drift_scan(repo). No secrets, no values, no probe transcripts restated from prior receipts. No AddMcpServer for Greptime. services/** untouched. Second tip: five Greptile P1s (4141814747, 4141814758, 4141814773, 4141814784, 4141814794) all verified as real and fixed — the JSON receipt was being swallowed by .gitignore, ls-remote had no timeout, an empty or malformed reachability target list exited 0, and the unit's TimeoutStartSec plus the timer's RandomizedDelaySec were fixed literals that broke the cadence guarantee. Third tip: Greptile P1 4141898005 (an unattempted git lookup reporting success) verified and fixed at the root — both *_TIMEOUT_S values are now validated before any probe runs, and 'never ran' is separated from 'ran and failed' in both sub-probes. The same defect was found and fixed in the reachability probe, which Greptile had not flagged. Head branch renamed to bot-05-infrastructure/* so G-1 can attribute the change. Fourth tip (LEAD GO, PR #38 after #36 was closed by the head-branch rename): INFRA unit sketch for the lease sweeper — substrate-lease-reap.{service,timer} calling the SYSTEMS-owned coord_reap_leases on the loopback substrate-mcp, default 45s within a 30-60s band, with the bearer kept in a root-only curl config file so no credential reaches the unit or a process listing. On-demand reaping through the MCP tool is retained and stays SYSTEMS'; the timer is only a sweeper for quiet load. Fifth tip: eight more Greptile findings on #38, all verified real and all fixed — leading zeros breaking the probe's unquoted JSON numbers (durations and ports), an empty target entry from a stray comma vanishing from the scan, EnvironmentFile optional on both units, Persistent= promising a catch-up tick a monotonic timer never delivers, the cron sketch both ignoring LEASE_INTERVAL_S above 60 and sourcing the env file as shell, the cadence invariant missing its TIMEOUT term because OnUnitActiveSec measures from renewal START not finish, and the receipt citing superseded PR #36. Sixth tip: Greptile P1 4142018423 — a failed sweep looked successful because curl --fail-with-body only checks the HTTP status while MCP reports tool failure as HTTP 200 with result.isError or a JSON-RPC error. ExecStart is now an INFRA-owned wrapper, substrate-lease-reap.sh, that parses the response (JSON or SSE) and exits non-zero unless the tool actually ran and succeeded. Seventh tip: two more findings on the wrapper itself — a multiline SSE result made a successful sweep exit 4 (parsed per data: line instead of joining the event's data as the SSE spec requires), and a negative SUBSTRATE_LEASE_REAP_LOG_BYTES inverted the journal cap into near-unbounded output. Both reproduced and fixed.

Every path this change touches, including both receipt files, resolves to bot-05-infrastructure (G-1 PASS). ownership.yaml itself was not edited: its bare README.md rule sends a README at any depth to QUALITY, so the two prose files are named SUBSTRATE-ENV.md and LEASE-HEARTBEAT.md instead.

drift-probe.sh is syntactically valid bash.
The git-tip probe reports local tip, branch, dirty flag, remote tip and the ahead/behind relation without fetching, and correctly resolved 'ahead' against origin/main.
The reachability probe distinguishes an open port, a closed port and a malformed target in one run, and a closed port does not abort the remaining probes.

Greptile P1 4141814747 confirmed, not refuted: .gitignore line 5 (.receipts/**/*.json) silently excluded the JSON receipt from the first commit, so the PR carried only the Markdown half and G-2 would have found no receipt for this task.
The JSON receipt is now tracked in git, force-added past that ignore rule the way the seat's existing .json receipts are. .gitignore itself is unowned in ownership.yaml, so it was not edited.
Greptile P1 4141814758 reproduced: a bare git ls-remote against an unresponsive remote does not return on its own and had to be killed by an outer cap.
With DRIFT_GIT_TIMEOUT_S the same lookup returns bounded, reports the timeout in 'note', and keeps exit 0 because a timed-out remote is a probe result rather than a probe that could not be attempted.
Greptile P1 4141814773 fixed for the empty case: an empty target list now exits 3 with ok:false instead of exiting 0 with an empty target array.
Greptile P1 4141814773 fixed for the malformed case: a malformed target is counted and exits 3, while the well-formed target beside it is still probed and reported.
A fully well-formed run still exits 0 and reports an open port up and a closed port down, so tightening the configuration checks did not turn an ordinary outage into a script failure.
Greptile P1 4141814794 and 4141814784 addressed in the units: TimeoutStartSec and RandomizedDelaySec are both marked PLACEHOLDER and generated at install time alongside OnUnitActiveSec.
Greptile P1 4141898005 confirmed, and worse than reported: on the pushed tip an invalid DRIFT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S also produced UNPARSEABLE JSON (timeout_s:abc emitted unquoted) while still exiting 0.
Root cause fixed at the source: both *_TIMEOUT_S values are validated before any probe runs, and a bad one stops the run with a config object and exit 3 instead of a misleading result.
A git lookup that could not be STARTED now reports ok:false with remote_checked:false and exits 3, so a caller trusting 'ok' can no longer read an unchecked remote tip as a completed check.
The same defect in the reachability probe is fixed: a connect that could not be started reports probed:false and is counted in targets_unattempted rather than claiming the target is down.
The ordinary paths still behave after the tightening: a good run exits 0 with remote_checked true, an open port up and a closed port down.
A timed-out remote is still treated as a probe result rather than a failure: ok stays true, remote_checked is false, and the exit stays 0.

substrate-lease-reap.sh is syntactically valid bash.
